elements.element: Customer has no minimum purchase or volume commitment.
elements.evidence: The redline expressly preserves a minimum: "Customer's commitment to any minimum monthly fee (including the Monthly Base Fee) is limited to the then-current twelve (12) month period", and the Monthly Base Fee minimum and ACH auto-debit language in the fee paragraphs are retained unchanged. The drafter targeted the fallback, not the preferred level.

elements.element: Customer pays only for usage or ordered Services.
elements.evidence: Retained language still requires "All minimum monthly fees (including the Monthly Base Fee) ... due in advance on the first day of the calendar month", i.e. payment irrespective of actual usage, subject only to a 12-month cap and true-up.

elements.element: The commitment is limited to the current 12-month term.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause: "Customer's commitment to any minimum monthly fee (including the Monthly Base Fee) is limited to the then-current twelve (12) month period of the Term", displacing the eight-year Term exposure created by the "Term" definition and the advance-payment sentence.

elements.element: Customer may reduce the commitment on 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: "[A]nd Customer may reduce that commitment, and the corresponding minimum monthly fees, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to M&I" — an unconditional Customer election, 30 days, written notice, applied to the minimum fee commitment itself.

elements.element: Any shortfall is handled through a true-up rather than a penalty.
elements.evidence: "Any shortfall between a minimum monthly fee and the fees for Services actually used shall be settled solely by a true-up payment of the difference, and not by any penalty." The basis (difference between minimum and fees for Services actually used) and the exclusion of penalties are both express.

elements.element: Any shortfall is handled through a true-up rather than a penalty.
elements.evidence: Not a preferred element; listed only to record that the preferred checklist (no minimum at all) is unmet because a minimum fee with a true-up mechanic is retained.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: the single inserted "Minimum Commitment" clause delivers all three fallback elements in operative terms (12-month limit on the minimum fee commitment, unconditional 30 days' written notice reduction right, shortfall settled solely by true-up and not by penalty). Preferred level is correctly not claimed, since a minimum monthly fee survives.

Minimality holds: nothing is deleted, the Customer-favourable prorating, invoicing and Fee Schedule mechanics are retained, and the insertion adds no survival tail, expense allocation, remedy or procedure beyond the three elements. The phrase "and the corresponding minimum monthly fees" is operationally necessary to make the reduction right bite on the amount payable, not an extra requirement.

Intent is preserved: the termination-fee and convenience-termination mechanics are untouched (correctly left to the T4C rule), and the sole-sourcing obligation in paragraph A (obtain all bundled Services from M&I during the Term) is left in place — that is an exclusivity term for a different rule, not a minimum-fee commitment, so leaving it is right and does not create a contradiction with the new fee-commitment cap.

Repair to verify before sending: the cross-reference "Notwithstanding Section 10.3(A)" is not corroborated by the cited text. The adjacent retained subsection is labelled "A." and points to Schedule 6.2, and the minimum monthly fee sentences sit in the charges/payment section. Confirm the number, or replace with a description (e.g. "Notwithstanding any other provision of this Agreement relating to minimum monthly fees") so the override cannot be read as a dangling reference.

Optional practical note (not a checklist defect): because paragraph A still requires Customer to obtain all bundled Monthly Base Fee Services from M&I for the eight-year Term, M&I may argue the reduction right cannot be exercised in practice. If we want belt-and-braces, address that under the exclusivity rule rather than by expanding this clause.
